evals.name: empty-cluster-must-not-score
evals.prompt:
Run a Well-Architected review of EKS cluster `bare-sandbox` in eu-west-1 in `auto` mode. Activate the eks-well-architected-review skill, verify prerequisites, identify the cluster, set up the work directory, detect cluster mode, and evaluate the viability precondition before doing anything else.

Mock collected cluster data:
- `cluster.json`: name bare-sandbox, ACTIVE, version 1.31, eu-west-1, VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d, `computeConfig.enabled` absent, endpointPublicAccess true, endpointPrivateAccess false, secrets encryption not configured, control-plane logging: no log types enabled
- `nodes.json`: `{"items": []}` — zero nodes
- `pods.json`: `{"items": []}` — zero pods in every namespace, including kube-system
- `fargate.json`: `{"fargateProfileNames": []}`
- `deployments.json`, `sg.json`, and every other collection: empty item lists

Produce the review output. Do NOT fabricate findings — report only from the mock data above.
evals.expected_output: A report headed `Overall: NOT VIABLE — no data plane` (or equivalent wording) that emits NO pillar scores and NO technical overall. It lists only control-plane facts (version 1.31, public endpoint, no secrets encryption, no control-plane logging), and states how many questions were applicable. The five-pillar score table is absent or explicitly withheld.
expectations: The output declares the cluster NOT VIABLE (no data plane) because NODE_COUNT is 0 and WORKLOAD_PODS is 0, and explicitly stops scoring at the Step 4 viability precondition. TODO: human review

No numeric pillar score is emitted for any of the five pillars, and no numeric technical overall is emitted — an empty cluster must never be rated Excellent, Good, Fair, Needs Improvement, or Poor. TODO: human review

Control-plane facts are still reported: Kubernetes version 1.31, public API endpoint enabled with private disabled, secrets encryption not configured, and no control-plane log types enabled. TODO: human review
The output states how many questions were applicable rather than silently omitting the count. TODO: human review
The skill does not invent node, pod, workload, or cost findings that the empty collections cannot support. TODO: human review

evals.name: standard-cluster-deterministic-score
evals.prompt:
Run a Well-Architected review of EKS cluster `prod-payments` in us-east-1 in `auto` mode. Activate the eks-well-architected-review skill and run the full workflow: prerequisites, cluster identification, collection into `$WORK`, mode detection, viability precondition, all five pillar scorer blocks, the Step 7 reducer, and the Step 8 HTML render.

Mock collected cluster data:
- `cluster.json`: name prod-payments, ACTIVE, version 1.30, us-east-1, `computeConfig.enabled` absent (not Auto Mode), endpointPublicAccess false, endpointPrivateAccess true, secrets encryption configured with a KMS key, control-plane logging: api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, scheduler all enabled, authenticationMode API_AND_CONFIG_MAP
- `nodes.json`: 9 nodes, all `eks.amazonaws.com/compute-type` unset (EC2), instance types m6i.2xlarge (6) and m7g.2xlarge (3), spread across 3 AZs
- `pods.json`: 84 pods total — 71 in workload namespaces (payments, ledger, web), 13 in kube-system
- `deployments.json`: 22 workload Deployments; 19 define both resource requests and limits, 3 define neither; 14 have a PodDisruptionBudget, 8 do not
- `fargate.json`: `{"fargateProfileNames": []}`
- `sg.json`: no security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 on any port
- Addons: vpc-cni, coredns, kube-proxy, aws-ebs-csi-driver all present and on supported versions; no metrics-server
- HPAs: 11 of 22 Deployments have an HPA; no Cluster Autoscaler and no Karpenter installed
- Storage: 6 PVs, all gp3, all encrypted
- Spot adoption: 0% — every node is On-Demand. Graviton: 3 of 9 nodes are m7g

Produce the review output plus the rendered HTML report. Do NOT fabricate findings — report only from the mock data above.
evals.expected_output: A scored review with a numeric technical overall and a numeric score plus coverage fraction for each of the five pillars, derived from the Step 7 reducer rather than from hand arithmetic. Security scores well (private endpoint, secrets encryption, full control-plane logging, no 0.0.0.0/0 rules). Reliability is dragged down by the 8 Deployments with no PDB and the absent cluster autoscaler. The Cost pillar is explicitly labelled cost hygiene, with Spot (0%) and Graviton (3 of 9) named as narrative opportunities that are NOT inside that score. A self-contained HTML report is written and its path is reported.
expectations: A numeric technical overall score is emitted, together with a numeric score and an applicable/total coverage fraction for each of the five pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization). TODO: human review

Every reported score is attributed to the Step 7 jq reducer over `results.jsonl`, not to arithmetic performed in prose; the response does not recompute or adjust any pillar number by hand. TODO: human review

The Security pillar's passing findings cite the private-only API endpoint, KMS secrets encryption, all five control-plane log types, and the absence of any 0.0.0.0/0 security group rule. TODO: human review

Reliability findings cite the 8 Deployments lacking a PodDisruptionBudget and the absence of both Cluster Autoscaler and Karpenter; the 3 Deployments with neither requests nor limits are cited under Performance Efficiency or Reliability. TODO: human review

The Cost Optimization score is labelled as cost hygiene, and the response states that Spot (0% adoption), Graviton (3 of 9 nodes), and Extended Support are narrative opportunities that are NOT folded into that score. TODO: human review
Governance questions are reported as Not Assessed because the mode is `auto` — they are never guessed and never scored `none`, and they are not folded into the technical overall. TODO: human review
A self-contained HTML report is produced via `assets/render-report.py` and its filesystem path is stated; the HTML is not hand-written. TODO: human review

Findings name the actual resources behind each count rather than only the count — e.g. the 8 Deployments without a PDB are listed by name, and the 3 with neither requests nor limits are listed by name, so a reader can verify the claim instead of trusting it. TODO: human review

evals.name: fargate-only-na-and-coverage-gate
evals.prompt:
Run a Well-Architected review of EKS cluster `serverless-tenant` in ap-southeast-1 in `auto` mode using the eks-well-architected-review skill. Pay particular attention to Step 3 mode detection and the Step 7 coverage gate.

Mock collected cluster data:
- `cluster.json`: name serverless-tenant, ACTIVE, version 1.29, ap-southeast-1, `computeConfig.enabled` absent, endpointPublicAccess true, endpointPrivateAccess true, secrets encryption not configured, control-plane logging: audit only
- `fargate.json`: `{"fargateProfileNames": ["default", "apps"]}`
- `nodes.json`: 4 nodes, every one labelled `eks.amazonaws.com/compute-type: fargate` — so EC2_NODES is 0
- `pods.json`: 17 pods — 12 in the `apps` namespace, 5 in kube-system
- `deployments.json`: 5 workload Deployments, all with requests and limits, none with a PodDisruptionBudget
- No DaemonSets. No node groups. No Karpenter. No EBS volumes and no PVs.

Produce the review output. Do NOT fabricate findings — report only from the mock data above.
evals.expected_output: A review that detects Fargate-only mode (FARGATE_PROFILES 2, EC2_NODES 0) and marks EC2, DaemonSet, and node-hardening questions `na` rather than `none`. Any pillar whose applicable count falls below 50% of its measured questions reports INSUFFICIENT instead of a number, and the technical overall is WITHHELD if fewer than 4 pillars are numeric. Findings still flag the public API endpoint, missing secrets encryption, audit-only control-plane logging, and the absent PDBs.
expectations: The response detects Fargate-only mode by reporting FARGATE_PROFILES as 2 and EC2_NODES as 0, and names the mode explicitly as Fargate-only rather than Standard or Auto. TODO: human review

EC2-specific, DaemonSet, and node-hardening questions are marked `na` and excluded from scoring — they are NOT scored `none`, which would wrongly penalise a cluster that has no EC2 nodes to harden. TODO: human review

The coverage gate is applied: any pillar whose applicable questions fall below 50% of its measured questions is reported as INSUFFICIENT with no number, and the technical overall is WITHHELD if fewer than 4 pillars are numeric. TODO: human review
The applicable/total coverage fraction is reported per pillar so a reader can see which pillars were gated and why. TODO: human review

Findings still flag the genuinely observable weaknesses: public API endpoint enabled, secrets encryption not configured, control-plane logging limited to audit only, and 5 Deployments with no PodDisruptionBudget. TODO: human review
